Cache invalidation in django CMS is broad: entire page caches are

A cache invalidation tag system is implemented. Every content
object (Page, PageContent, Placeholder, CMSPlugin) has associated
cache tags. When an object is created, updated, or deleted, its
cache tags are invalidated. The system consists of:
  - a relevant module: Utility functions for generating cache tags
    (make_tag, get_tags_for_object) and invalidating by tag
    (invalidate_by_tag).
  - a relevant module: Signal handlers connected to post_save and
    post_delete of Page, PageContent, Placeholder, CMSPlugin that
    call invalidate_by_tag with the object's tags.
  - a relevant module: Update CMSToolbarMiddleware (or a new
    middleware) to tag response objects with the cache tags of
    rendered content.
  - a relevant module: Update {% placeholder %} and
    related tags to check cache using the tag system before
    rendering.
The system must be opt-in: existing cache behavior is preserved
if the new tag system is not configured.

- The change must be implemented correctly

- The cache backend must be configurable (default: Django's
default cache).

- Tag-based cache checking must be a performance improvement,
not a degradation: use a single cache get with tag lookup
rather than multiple round-trips.
